chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rabi'i ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the man bares the slave girl and places his hand upon her, she is not permitted for his son.

key_terms.جَرَّدَ: To bare or strip naked; a technical term in fiqh referring to the act of a man having sexual intercourse with or fully exposing his female slave.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a son marrying his father's slave girl after the father has bared her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'jarrada' (exposing or intimate contact) as a form of consummation that creates a prohibition similar to marriage, preventing the father and son from marrying the same slave girl. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the legal weight of physical intimacy in establishing familial bonds, extending the prohibition beyond formal contract to include significant physical acts. It highlights the distinct treatment of slave women in early Islamic law, where intimate relations with a father could bar the son from marrying her, preserving lineage clarity and familial honor.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the man bares the slave girl and places his hand upon her, so she would not be Permitted unto his father’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Rib’iy ibn ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a man makes a slave-girl bare and places his hand on her she becomes unlawful for his son.’”
